title: Cafe Negril
venue_description:
Frenchmen Street's Live Music Institution

Cafe Negril has been a cornerstone of New Orleans' legendary Frenchmen Street music scene long before the street gained worldwide recognition. This venue embodies the authentic spirit of New Orleans music showcasing local talent across multiple genres every night of the week.

Musical Diversity

The venue features an eclectic mix of musical styles that reflect New Orleans' rich cultural heritage. From reggae and R&B to blues funk jazz and rock and roll Cafe Negril provides a platform for the city's finest musicians. Regular performers include Higher Heights Reggae one of the city's most beloved reggae and R&B bands; John Lisi & Delta Funk delivering slamming funky blues; Jamey St. Pierre & THC a resident singer-songwriter for over a decade; and Jason Neville Funky Soul Band led by the youngest son of 5x Grammy winner Aaron Neville.

The Tuesday Blues Jam

Every Tuesday Cafe Negril hosts the Super-Most-Fantastic-Blues-N-Such-Jam led by guitar legend John Lisi and the Delta Funk band. This open jam session welcomes musicians to bring their instruments and vocals to participate. Multiple sets run throughout the evening starting at 7:00 PM with the house band providing solid backing for jammers. The format is welcoming to players at various skill levels who want to explore blues funk and related styles.

Wednesday Jam Session

Wednesday nights feature Jam-ilton an innovative concept where vocals are reimagined on saxophone and supported by a funky New Orleans rhythm section. The format encourages participation - whether you want to jam on stage or dance on the floor all are welcome. This event brings new grooves to familiar favorites from funk to pop.

Venue Layout and Seating

Cafe Negril offers multiple seating options to enhance the live music experience. Ground floor high-top tables and stools provide close proximity to the action and easy access to the dance floor. The elevated VIP section features light-up tables and cubes with optimal sightlines for viewing performances. Reserved seating is available through advance ticket purchase though walk-ins are also accommodated based on availability.

Atmosphere and Vibe

The venue maintains an authentic New Orleans character with vibrant murals reflecting the city's cultural richness. The space balances intimacy with energy - large enough for dancing but cozy enough for genuine connection with the music. The sound quality is excellent and performers are visible from throughout the space. Between sets the venue maintains a lively social atmosphere where locals and visitors mix freely.

Food and Beverage

The venue serves a selection of food including tacos burritos and pizza. The bar offers a full selection of drinks with a two-drink minimum enforced for shows. Specialty cocktails local beers and standard bar offerings are available. The venue is 21+ only as required by law.

Performance Schedule

Live music happens seven nights a week with multiple showtimes each evening. Most nights feature 2-3 different sets with showtimes typically beginning in the afternoon or early evening and continuing past midnight on weekends. The venue livestreams performances on their YouTube channel allowing music lovers to enjoy shows remotely.

Special Events

Beyond regular programming Cafe Negril hosts parade watch parties during Mardi Gras season including the Krewe du Vieux and Red Beans Parade. These events feature live music special menus and front-row seating for viewing parades that pass directly in front of the venue. Valentine's Day and other special occasions bring unique collaborative shows featuring multiple bands.

Musician Support

The venue operates with deep respect for musicians encouraging patrons to tip performers generously. After each set band members or designated collectors circulate through the audience to collect tips directly. This direct support model ensures musicians are compensated for their talent and hard work maintaining New Orleans' tradition of supporting live music.

Practical Information

Seating is available for reservation through the venue's ticketing system with tickets typically priced affordably. Tickets are valid for specific time blocks typically 90 minutes. The venue accommodates groups but requests that parties of 10 or more call ahead at (504) 229-4236. Optional add-ons include balloon drops and personalized messages displayed on screens for celebrations.

History and Legacy

Cafe Negril established itself on Frenchmen Street well before the area became a tourist destination. The venue has provided a launching pad for countless local musicians who got their start on its stage. This commitment to supporting emerging and established local talent has made Cafe Negril an essential part of New Orleans' musical ecosystem. The venue represents the authentic spirit of Frenchmen Street - a place where music is the priority where locals and visitors connect through shared appreciation of New Orleans' musical heritage.

title: Another Bar
venue_description:
Freret Street's Eclectic Community Hub

Another Bar stands as a vibrant and welcoming dive bar in the heart of New Orleans' Freret Street corridor. More than just a drinking establishment it serves as a genuine community gathering place where locals and visitors connect through music games and creative expression.

Thursday Open Mic

Every Thursday at 8:00 PM Another Bar hosts a weekly open mic for music and poetry. Hosted by Duane Bartels the event welcomes all forms of musical and spoken word performance. The venue provides basic PA equipment for performers. Sign-ups happen on the spot maintaining an accessible and spontaneous atmosphere.

Additional Entertainment

Beyond Thursday's open mic the venue offers diverse weekly entertainment. Sunday nights feature karaoke providing another outlet for musical expression in a supportive environment. Tuesday nights host Not Another Open Mic comedy showcase starting at 8:30 PM which is free to attend. The venue regularly features various themed gatherings that cater to different community interests.

Games and Activities

Another Bar distinguishes itself with an array of games and activities. Board games are available throughout the venue including the popular drunk Jenga that regulars enjoy. Skee ball provides arcade-style entertainment. These activities create a relaxed social atmosphere where patrons can enjoy themselves whether or not live entertainment is happening.

Atmosphere and Character

The space features eclectic and artsy decor that reflects the creative spirit of the Freret Street neighborhood. Picnic-style seating creates a casual comfortable environment. The venue attracts a diverse and friendly crowd - from students and artists to neighborhood regulars and adventurous visitors exploring beyond the French Quarter.

Bar Program

The bar specializes in affordable mojitos and features Canebrake on tap among other beverage options. Drink prices are notably reasonable making the venue accessible for those seeking a fun night out without breaking the bank. However the venue does not allow open tabs - each tab must be closed after every visit so patrons should plan accordingly.

Hours of Operation

Another Bar operates Monday through Thursday from 4:00 PM to midnight Friday and Saturday from 4:00 PM to 2:00 AM and Sunday from 4:00 PM to midnight. The extended weekend hours accommodate the neighborhood's active nightlife while maintaining reasonable closing times during the week.

The Freret Street Context

Located at 5039 Freret Street the venue sits in a neighborhood that has undergone significant revitalization in recent years. Freret Street has transformed into a thriving local hub featuring diverse restaurants bars and shops. Another Bar participates thoughtfully in this evolution maintaining authentic dive bar character while serving as an accessible community space.

Accessibility and Transportation

The Freret Street location is well-served by public transportation and provides easier parking than downtown or French Quarter venues. This accessibility makes it a convenient option for locals from various neighborhoods. The venue is fully accessible for individuals with mobility challenges.

Staff and Service

Patrons consistently praise the outstanding service provided by the skilled bartenders. The staff creates a welcoming atmosphere where everyone feels like part of the family. Bartenders craft creative cocktails while ensuring genuine hospitality. This attention to service contributes significantly to the venue's reputation as a beloved local spot.

Community Values

Another Bar operates with strong community values fostering an environment of kindness and acceptance. The venue welcomes diverse patrons and creates space for self-expression through various artistic and social outlets. This inclusive approach has built a loyal following of regulars who appreciate both the entertainment and the welcoming vibe.

title: Prytania Bar
venue_description:
Garden District Neighborhood Watering Hole

The Prytania Bar is a simple laid-back neighborhood establishment located on the cusp of New Orleans' historic Garden District. With its distinctive 360-degree bar providing ample seating and unpretentious atmosphere this venue has served locals and visitors for years as a reliable gathering spot.

Open Mic Nights

Every other Friday at 9:00 PM The Prytania Bar hosts an open mic night led by host Tim Curry. The venue provides a small stage area (not raised) with a 4-channel PA system two microphones and mic stands. This basic but functional setup accommodates acoustic and light electric performances. The bi-weekly schedule ensures consistent programming while allowing the venue to maintain its regular bar atmosphere on alternating Fridays.

Live Music Programming

Beyond open mic nights The Prytania Bar features occasional live music performances throughout the week. The venue focuses on local talent providing a platform for New Orleans musicians to perform in a casual supportive environment. The intimate setting allows for genuine connection between performers and audience.

Bar Specialties

The bar takes pride in offering Southern Regional Craft beers on tap showcasing breweries from across the region. The drink menu features fun cocktails spicy Bloody Marys (a particular specialty available for $5 on weekends from 11am-7pm) and The Iced Irish Coffee - the venue's most popular beverage. This signature drink combines Irish whiskey coffee and cream in a refreshing iced format perfect for New Orleans' warm climate.

Weekly Events and Specials

Wednesdays bring trivia night at 7:30 PM where teams compete for a $50 bar tab and other prizes. Following trivia a Hump Day Happy Hour runs from 11pm-2am featuring $3 draft beer and $3 Jager/Jameson/Fireball shots. This late-night special caters to service industry workers and night owls.

Daily Drink Specials

Monday features $2 domestic beers all day long. Tuesday offers $2 well liquor wines and champagne throughout the day. Thursday and Friday run happy hour from 4-8pm with $1 off all draft beer and liquor. Saturday and Sunday showcase the $5 Big Bloody Mary special from 11am-7pm perfect for brunch or afternoon drinking.

Seasonal Events

During crawfish season (typically March through May) The Prytania Bar hosts Crawfish Fridays from 5-8pm featuring $10 All You Can Eat Crawfish paired with $3 Lagunitas IPA. This popular event celebrates Louisiana's beloved crustacean and draws crowds of locals and visitors eager to experience this regional delicacy.

Atmosphere and Clientele

The Prytania Bar maintains a genuine dive bar atmosphere without pretension. The 360-degree bar encourages social interaction making it easy for solo patrons to strike up conversations with neighbors. Sports play on TV screens throughout the space though the volume is kept reasonable to allow conversation. The crowd includes a mix of Garden District residents students from nearby universities and visitors exploring beyond the French Quarter.

Location and Accessibility

Situated at 3445 Prytania Street the bar occupies a prime location on the edge of the Garden District one of New Orleans' most beautiful and historic neighborhoods. The location provides easier parking than downtown venues while remaining accessible to various neighborhoods. Street parking is typically available on Prytania Street and surrounding blocks.

Hours of Operation

The bar operates Monday through Thursday from 3:00 PM to 1:00 AM Friday from 3:00 PM to 2:00 AM Saturday from 10:30 AM to 2:00 AM (to accommodate brunch crowds) and Sunday from 11:30 AM to midnight. These hours reflect the neighborhood's character - late enough for nightlife but not extreme closing times.

Social Media and Updates

Patrons can follow @ThePrytaniaBar on social media platforms including Twitter and Instagram for current events specials and schedule updates. This digital presence helps regular customers stay informed about live music bookings special events and any schedule changes.

title: Ashe Cultural Arts Center
venue_description:
Celebrating African and African American Culture

Ashe Cultural Arts Center stands as a vital institution dedicated to preserving and promoting African and African American culture through the arts in New Orleans. Located at 1719 Oretha Castle Haley Boulevard the center provides essential space for artists cultural practitioners and community members to gather create and celebrate.

Adinkra Lounge Open Mic

The center's Adinkra Lounge hosts monthly open mic nights typically on Friday evenings from 7:00 PM to 11:00 PM. These events welcome creative expression in all forms - from seasoned performers to first-timers stepping on stage for the first time. The open mic is free and open to the public with doors opening at 7:00 PM and the mic opening at 7:30 PM. Performers can sign up on the spot maintaining an accessible and spontaneous format.

Mission and Programs

Ashe Cultural Arts Center operates with a clear mission to be a catalyst for cultural equity and social change through the arts. The organization provides multidisciplinary arts programming educational initiatives and community events that center African and African American cultural traditions while remaining relevant to contemporary experiences.

Community Impact

The center serves as a gathering place where culture creativity and community intersect. Through various programs and events Ashe creates opportunities for artistic growth cultural preservation and community building. The organization recognizes that the arts serve not just as entertainment but as essential tools for cultural expression education and social transformation.

The Oretha Castle Haley Corridor

Located on the historic Oretha Castle Haley Boulevard (formerly Dryades Street) the center occupies a significant position in a corridor undergoing cultural and economic revitalization. This area has deep historical importance in New Orleans' African American community and Ashe plays a central role in honoring that legacy while contributing to the neighborhood's ongoing evolution.

Performance Space

The Adinkra Lounge provides an intimate supportive environment for performances. The space features appropriate sound reinforcement for various artistic expressions while maintaining the warmth and community feel that characterizes the center's approach. The atmosphere encourages risk-taking and authentic expression recognizing that art thrives when creators feel supported and valued.

Accessibility and Inclusion

Ashe Cultural Arts Center operates with strong commitment to accessibility and inclusion. Events are designed to welcome participants from throughout New Orleans regardless of economic means with many programs offered free or at minimal cost. This approach ensures that cultural participation isn't limited by financial barriers honoring the principle that culture belongs to the community.
location: 1719 Oretha Castle Haley Blvd New Orleans LA 70113
